prediction.likelyOutcome: Barham will almost certainly recover at least the $163,000 appraised value, since the taking itself is uncontested and some compensation is owed as a matter of law. The real fight — and the case's true value driver — is whether the jury treats the Threel Road access loss as a compensable taking of an easement/change in property use (potentially pushing the award well above $163,000) or as non-compensable circuity of travel given the available Aronson Road access, an outcome made harder to predict without knowing what, if anything, Barham already recovered in the separate County Line Action.

issues.label: Just Compensation for the Direct Taking (Fee Strip, Access-Control Line, Temporary ROW)
Compensability of Threel Road Easement Loss (Traffic-Flow vs. Easement Taking)
Double-Recovery / Prior Adjudication in the County Line Action

outcome.description: After a May 2022 jury trial the Marion Circuit Court entered judgment on a $2.4 million verdict for Barham and denied Carmel's motions to correct error, for new trial, and for remittitur. The Court of Appeals reversed on October 30, 2023, holding Barham had no compensable easement interest in Threel Road (already extinguished in the County Line condemnation) and that the access change was non-compensable under the ingress-egress and traffic-flow rules, and remanded with instructions to grant Carmel partial summary judgment on that issue.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed and remanded; no final figure yet.
